chunks: Muhammad b. Ahmad b. Ali b. Asad al-Asadi narrated to us. He said: Ya'qub b. Yusuf b. Hazim narrated to us. He said: Umar b. Ismail b. Mujalid narrated to us. He said: Hafs b. Ghiyath narrated to us from Burd b. Sinan from Makhul from Wathila b. al-Asqa'. He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Do not display gloating over the misfortune of your brother, or else Allah will have mercy on him and cause you tribulation.

key_terms.الشماتة: Schadenfreude or gloating over the misfortune of others; considered a grave moral failing in Islam
key_terms.يبتليك: To afflict or test; God may redirect the same trial to the one who gloated

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about gloating over others' misfortune?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) prohibited gloating (shamatah) over the misfortune of a fellow Muslim, warning that such behavior may lead God to show mercy to the afflicted person while sending trials upon the one who gloats. This teaching, transmitted through the companion Wathila b. al-Asqa', emphasizes that believers must maintain empathy and compassion toward one another, and that schadenfreude is not only morally reprehensible but may provoke divine retribution.
word_analysis: so He will have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. Ahmad b. `Ali b. Asad al-Asadi narrated to us. He said: Ya`qub b. Yusuf b. Hazim narrated to us. He said: `Umar b. Isma`il b. Mujalid narrated to us. He said: Hafs b. Ghiyath narrated to us from Bard b. Sinan from Makhul from Wathila b. al-Ashqa`.  He said: The Messenger of Allah (s) said:
Do not gloat over the misfortune of your brother, or else Allah will have mercy on him and cause you tribulation.
